stories.headline: RBI steps up checks on importers' forex deals near $2 million
points: RBI has increased scrutiny of importers' forex transactions over concerns that deals may be split below $2 million.
The worry is that firms may be doing this to avoid additional reserve requirements.
Average dollar-buying deal sizes have fallen sharply since October 10, while the number of deals has risen.
stories.why_it_matters: Forex rules and thresholds affect compliance and audit work, especially for banks and companies that handle import payments.
stories.source_title: RBI hunts for possible '$2 million loophole' in importers' forex transactions
check_notes: The 'Why it matters' line mentions 'audit work' and gives general context that the source doesn't state. It is framed as analysis, not as a reported fact.

The third point closely follows the source's wording ('sharp fall in average dollar-buying transaction sizes since October 10, even as the number of deals has risen'). It is paraphrased rather than copied, but it is close.
The headline says 'near $2 million', but the source says deals may be split to come in below the $2 million threshold. This is a small wording difference and does not mislead.
The story leaves out that RBI's move led to fresh compliance checks on banks. This is a missing detail, not an error.

stories.headline: ITAT Delhi deletes ₹51.15 lakh penalty after 14A disallowance set aside
points: For AY 2014–15, the AO disallowed ₹1,70,48,420 under section 14A and later levied a ₹51,14,629 penalty under 271(1)(c).
The Tribunal sent the 14A issue back to the AO for fresh Rule 8D recomputation, so the original figure no longer stood.
The CIT(A) dismissed the penalty appeal as infructuous; the ITAT instead deleted the penalty, citing loss of its foundation.
stories.why_it_matters: Shows how penalty under section 271(1)(c) depends on the underlying addition, a key point in assessment and appeal work.
stories.source_title: Income Tax | ITAT Delhi: Section 271(1)(c) Penalty Unsustainable Once Section 14A Disallowance Is Set Aside

stories.headline: ITAT Raipur quashes reassessment over shortened return-filing period
points: ITAT Raipur held a Section 148 notice void if it gives less time to file a return than the Act allows.
The 29 March 2024 notice asked for a return within 90 days of issue; the Act gave three months from month-end.
The Tribunal called it a jurisdictional defect, quashed the reassessment for AY 2020-21 and allowed the appeal.
stories.why_it_matters: Shows how procedural details of a reassessment notice can decide its validity, a key point in income tax law and practice.
stories.source_title: Income Tax | ITAT Raipur: Section 148 Notice Void if Statutory Return Filing Period Is Shortened
